title: Deterministic Zeckendorf games: Split Smallest is Fibonacci-regular
statement: In the deterministic Zeckendorf games of Li, Li, Miller et al., every play has n - Z(n) merging moves and length sum_{i in Zeck(n)} c_i - sum over add-consecutive moves of (j - 2) (c_1 = 0, c_2 = 1, c_3 = 3, c_{i+1} = 2 c_i - c_{i-2} + 1). The Split Smallest split count is conjectured to be Fibonacci-regular, with an explicit 9-dimensional linear representation over Zeckendorf blocks that reproduces it for every n <= 120,000; its value at F_k and F_k - 1 is F_{k+1} - (2k^2 + 8k + 15 + (-1)^k)/8 (F_0 = 1, F_1 = 2), proved at F_k - 1 from Cusenza et al.; and S(F_k + m) - S(F_k) - S(m) depends only on m and the parity of k. Combine Smallest shows full Hankel rank in the tested window.
resolves: Li, Li, Miller et al. (2020) open question 'how long do the deterministic games take and who wins as a function of n' for Split Smallest, conjecturally, with an explicit finite representation
verified: For every n <= 3000 and all four deterministic games: n - Z(n) merging moves and the length identity hold, CL and SL have length n - Z(n), and SS equals the maximum game length computed over the full game graph for n <= 40.

The SS linear representation reproduces the SS split count for every n <= 120,000 (C simulator output, SHA-256 recorded), the Fibonacci closed form holds for every F_k <= 120,000, and the block law has no violation; perturbing one representation entry breaks agreement.
Hankel ranks over Zeckendorf words: SS 6, 6, 6 and CS 13, 21, 34 at word lengths 6, 7, 8; the CS length ratio is 1.206480 at n = 9,227,465.

Counter lemma (written proof, gated for 20,000 steps): while two 1's remain, each SS step moves the upper word to the radix-order successor in the language of binary words with no 00 except one final 00 followed only by 1's (the lazy Fibonacci representations plus a transient tail), making as many splits as the previous word has trailing 1's.
unresolved: a proof that the SS split count is Fibonacci-regular: the counting phase is proved (lazy Fibonacci counter); the end phase and the assembly into Zeckendorf digits remain
an exact description of Combine Smallest lengths, and a proof that they are not Fibonacci-regular
nonclaims: the length identity is a rewriting of Cusenza et al.'s exact move-count formula, not a new result
the SS regularity, block law and the closed form at F_k are verified in range, not proved
CS non-regularity is evidenced by Hankel rank growth, not proved
smallest_decisive_test: An n at which the Split Smallest split count differs from the 9-dimensional representation, or a proof of the block law.
